We will use the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=\frac{\frac{d}{d\theta }(\frac{dy}{dx})}{(\frac{dx}{d\theta })}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(2\theta ).$ Also, since $r=5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dx}{d\theta } & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ) \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting into our formula for the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\frac{d}{d\theta }(\operatorname{tan}⁡(2\theta ))}{5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )} \\  & =\frac{2{sec}^{2}⁡(2\theta )}{5\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}{sec}^{3}⁡(2\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
